Q: Scan directories and copy those that have more than n files A:

With bash you can:

  • use pathname expansion to loop over all artist directories: for a in *; do ...; done
  • use pathname expansion to collect all song files of an artist in an array: s=("$a"/*/*),
  • use its number of elements to decide to copy or not: ((${#s[@]} >= 7)) && cp ....

Example with a minimum of 7 songs and destination directory /tmp/sdcard. Adapt to your needs:

cd music &&
mkdir -p /tmp/sdcard &&
for a in *; do s=("$a"/*/*); ((${#s[@]} >= 7)) && cp -a "$a" /tmp/sdcard; done

Note: different from other solutions (including the accepted one) this works even if the names of some of your files contain spaces, newlines or other special characters, a frequent situation with audio files.

Note: if some directories or song files are hidden (.the_hidden_song.mp3) we must enable the dotglob option to catch them with the pathname expansions. And if some of the directories can be empty, also enabling the nullglob option is preferable. We do this in a subshell ( ... ) to automatically restore these two options to there original value when done:

(
shopt -s dotglob nullglob
cd music &&
mkdir -p /tmp/sdcard &&
for a in *; do s=("$a"/*/*); ((${#s[@]} >= 7)) && cp -a "$a" /tmp/sdcard; done
)

Q: Use "terra::predict" with a "quantregForest" model and get the standard deviation of predictions A:

I use a minimal, self-contained, reproducible example to facilitate answering your questions.

When using terra::predict with a quantregForest object, what=sd works. With a caret train object it is ignored because caret::predict.train does not forward what to quantregForest::predict.quantregForest.

Example data

library(terra)
logo <- rast(system.file("ex/logo.tif", package = "terra"))
set.seed(1)
s <- spatSample(logo, 200, "random", na.rm = TRUE, as.df = TRUE)
s$y <- with(s, 0.5 * red + 0.3 * green + 0.2 * blue + rnorm(nrow(s), 0, 10))

Fit a model and predict

library(quantregForest)
qrf <- quantregForest(x = s[, c("red", "green", "blue")], y = s$y,  ntree = 50)

# Same pattern as the glm se.fit custom fun example in ?terra::predict
predfun <- function(model, data, ...) {
  cbind(
    mean = predict(model, data, what = mean),
    sd   = predict(model, data, what = sd)
  )
}

out <- predict(logo, qrf, fun = predfun, na.rm = TRUE)
plot(out)

# Or the equivalent by passing what= through ... 
# (like se.fit=TRUE in the glm example)
sd_only <- predict(logo, qrf, na.rm=TRUE, what=sd)

If the fitted object is a caret train model, use model$finalModel (a quantregForest) instead (and you figured that out).

To use a categorical variable, you do not need to dummies or one-hot-encoding in this case. You can do

library(terra)
library(quantregForest)

flogo <- rast(system.file("ex/logo.tif", package = "terra"))
flogo$red <- classify(flogo$red, c(-1, 85, 170, 256)) 
# flogo$red is a factor, see as.factor for a pre-existing variable

set.seed(1)
dat <- spatSample(flogo, 300, "random", na.rm = TRUE, as.df = TRUE)
dat$y <- with(dat, 0.4 * as.numeric(red) + 0.3 * green + 0.2 * blue
               + rnorm(nrow(dat), 0, 8))

qrf_fac <- quantregForest(x = dat[, c("red", "green", "blue")],
                          y = dat$y, ntree = 400)
out_fac <- predict(flogo, qrf_fac, na.rm = TRUE, what = mean)

But you can...

## One-hot with terra::segregate (all 3 classes)
oh <- segregate(flogo$red)
names(oh) <- c("A", "B", "C")
ohlogo <- c(flogo[[2:3]], oh)

set.seed(1)
dat_oh <- spatSample(ohlogo, 300, "random", na.rm = TRUE)
dat_oh$y <- dat$y

qrf_oh <- quantregForest(x=dat_oh[, c("green", "blue", "A", "B", "C")], 
                         y=dat_oh$y, ntree = 400)
out_oh <- predict(ohlogo, qrf_oh, na.rm = TRUE, what = mean)

## Dummy encoding — drop reference class A
set.seed(1)
qrf_dum <- quantregForest(x=dat_oh[, c("green", "blue", "B", "C")], 
                          y=dat_oh$y, ntree = 400)
out_dum <- predict(ohlogo, qrf_dum, na.rm = TRUE, what = mean)

pairs(c(out_fac, out_oh, out_dum))

plot(rast(list(factor=out_fac, onehot=out_oh, dummy=out_dum)), 
          nr=1, mar=c(2,2,2,4))

Very similar results --- not the same, they are not the same models. One variable becomes two or three variables. I do not know why you get missing values. I expect it is because of name/level mismatches, or because there are values outside the training factor levels, not from omitting the reference class. Either way, I would not use the dummy encoding in this case.

Q: Scaffold vs Surface A:
  1. Difference between Scaffold and Surface?

  • Scaffold: a structural screen-layout for Material UI. (e.g.: TopBar, BottomBar, FAB, Snackbar, Content insets/padding)

  • Surface: a visual/theming container. (e.g.: Background color, text content coloring, Shape, Elevation, Border, Clipping, )

  1. What are the pros and cons of each?

  • pros:

    • Scaffold: Create relationships between bars, FABs, and content explicit.
    • Surface: lightweight, explicit and flexible (e.g.: cards, dialogs)

  • cons:

    • Scaffold: Overkill for sub-views, custom cards, or simple screens without app bars.
    • Surface: You need to handle spacing/insets yourself
  1. Common Best Practice?

Latest solution combines both at their respective architectural boundaries

  • Scaffold: Use it at the top level of individual screens level to organize layout slots and handle screen inset padding.

  • Surface: Wrap the entire solution theme in a root Surface (inside MaterialTheme) to establish the baseline background color and default text content color across the solution window.

Q: How to create boxplot graph and same coloured spots around them A:

Update on OP request:

The code:

library(ggpubr)


# create fake data mtcars1
mtcars1 <- mtcars %>% 
  add_row(mtcars[1,]) %>% 
  mutate(group = rep(c("A", "B", "C"), 11))

compare_means(disp ~ cyl, data = mtcars1,  method = "t.test")
my_comparisons <- list( c("4", "6"), c("6", "8"), c("4", "8") )

ggboxplot(mtcars1, x = "cyl", y = "disp", fill = "cyl", add = "jitter") +
  scale_fill_manual(values=c("#0433ff", "#fe403f", "#66cd00")) +
  stat_compare_means(comparisons = my_comparisons)+
  stat_compare_means(label.y = 700) +
  facet_grid(.~group, switch = "x")+
  xlab(NULL) +
  theme(strip.background = element_blank(),
        strip.placement = "outside")

Here is an example using the ggpubr package and the mtcars dataset:

library(ggpubr)

compare_means(disp ~ cyl, data = mtcars,  method = "t.test")
my_comparisons <- list( c("4", "6"), c("6", "8"), c("4", "8") )

ggboxplot(mtcars, x = "cyl", y = "disp", color = "cyl", add = "jitter") +
  stat_compare_means(comparisons = my_comparisons)+
  stat_compare_means(label.y = 700)

Q: Create a columns conditioned to two possible levels contained in another column A:

Please be so kind put the data in your posts. >> dput(df)

You could use a combination of case_when and str_detect

library(dplyr)
library(stringr) 

df <- structure(
      list(
    ID = 1:10,
    GROUP = rep('TRAINING', 10),
    Gender = rep(1, 10),
    Education = rep(74, 10),
    test =  c(
      'ADAS_CogT0',
      'ROCF_CT0',
      'ROCF_IT0',
      'ROCF_RT0',
      'PVF_T0',
      'SVF_T0',
      'ADAS_CogT7',
      'ROCF_CT7',
      'ROCF_IT7',
      'ROCF_RT7'
    ),
    score = c(14.7,32,3.7,3.9,41.3,40,16,33,1.7,2.4)
  ),
  row.names = c(1:10),
  class = "data.frame"
)

df2 <- df %>%
  mutate(new = case_when(str_detect(test, 'T0') ~ 'score0',
                         str_detect(test, 'T7') ~ 'score7',
                         TRUE ~ test)

Q: How to loop a function and save the outputs of each run as independent objects? A:

Use Map and assign the result to list L and then L$mpg etc can get individual components. Alternately use list2env to place the components of L into the global environment. Normally using a list is preferable to having loose objects in the global environment.

library(dplyr)
 
calculate_summary <- function(var) {
  mtcars %>% 
    dplyr::group_by(cyl, vs) %>% 
    dplyr::summarise(
      N = length(.data[[var]]),
      mean = mean(.data[[var]]),
      sd   = sd(.data[[var]]),
      se   = sd / sqrt(N),
      .groups = "drop")
}
 
 
L <- Map(calculate_summary, c("mpg", "qsec"))
L$mpg
## # A tibble: 5 × 6
##     cyl    vs     N  mean     sd     se
##   <dbl> <dbl> <int> <dbl>  <dbl>  <dbl>
## 1     4     0     1  26   NA     NA    
## 2     4     1    10  26.7  4.75   1.50 
## 3     6     0     3  20.6  0.751  0.433
## 4     6     1     4  19.1  1.63   0.816
## 5     8     0    14  15.1  2.56   0.684

or

list2env(L, globalenv())
<environment: R_GlobalEnv>

mpg
## # A tibble: 5 × 6
##     cyl    vs     N  mean     sd     se
##   <dbl> <dbl> <int> <dbl>  <dbl>  <dbl>
## 1     4     0     1  26   NA     NA    
## 2     4     1    10  26.7  4.75   1.50 
## 3     6     0     3  20.6  0.751  0.433
## 4     6     1     4  19.1  1.63   0.816
## 5     8     0    14  15.1  2.56   0.684

Another approach is to create a single data frame and then filter it:

library(dplyr)
library(purrr)

DF <- map_dfr(set_names(c("mpg", "qsec")), calculate_summary, .id = "group")
filter(DF, group == "mpg")
## # A tibble: 5 × 7
##   group   cyl    vs     N  mean     sd     se
##   <chr> <dbl> <dbl> <int> <dbl>  <dbl>  <dbl>
## 1 mpg       4     0     1  26   NA     NA    
## 2 mpg       4     1    10  26.7  4.75   1.50 
## 3 mpg       6     0     3  20.6  0.751  0.433
## 4 mpg       6     1     4  19.1  1.63   0.816
## 5 mpg       8     0    14  15.1  2.56   0.684

Q: RISC-V return address corruption bug A:

I managed to reproduce the issue using cocotb, a HDL testbench framework for cosimulation. I created a testbench that first loaded the ELF firmware image into TCM memory via the TAS (TCM access port), verified it and then triggered interrupts at different parts of the program. The breakthrough happened when I found, in the MiV RV32 release notes, that there was an issue with byte stores and interrupts in the past, so I focused the testbench testing on interrupting byte stores during different stages of the byte store state machine.
With this, I managed to actually reproduce the exact issue, matching the instruction pattern of the trace I posted in the question. My current understanding is that TCM only allows word access so a byte store requires read-modify-write and there seems to be some bug in the core that, when the RMW state machine is interrupted during a particular state, the follow-up write succeeds from the POV of the core, but no actual memory write happened.

I had enough information to open up a Microchip support case at this point, so I did. After some back and forth Microchip confirmed that there is a bug and that they expect a fix with the December 26 release of the MiV RV32 4.0.0 version.
In the meantime, the confirmed workaround is to duplicate the RA store instruction, or whichever store happens first in the interrupt handler. This is also what was previously used in the MiV RV32 HAL code to patch the issue mentioned in the release notes.
